description: A named piece of work with parameters, a return type and a body, called by its name with one argument per parameter.
A parameter is a named input in the method's declaration; an argument is the value passed for it at a call.
The type of the value a method hands back with `return`; `void` means the method returns no value.
A method whose body is a single expression written after `=>`, with no braces and no `return` keyword.
The region of code where a name exists; a variable declared inside a method cannot be used outside its braces.
One of several methods with the same name but different parameter lists, chosen by the compiler from the arguments.
A parameter with a default value may be left out at a call, and a named argument such as `rate: 0.06m` passes a value by parameter name in any order.
A method without a name written as a value, such as `x => x * 2`, with parameters left of `=>` and the result on the right.
